div.l: Vp on an ambler . all esily sche sat .
Wympled well . ⁊and on here heed an hat .
As brood as is a bokeler . or a targe .
A foot mantell . a boute here hipes large .
And on here feet . a paire of spores scharpe
In felawschipe . well couthe laugh ⁊and carpe .
Of remedies of loue . sche knewe ꝑperchaunce .
For sche couthe of that arte . the olde daūnce .
A Good man was there . of religioıı̄un
And was . a pore ꝑpersoūn of a toıı̄un .
But riche he was . of holy thought ⁊and werke .
He was also a lerned man ⁊and a Clerke .
And cristes gospell . trewely wolde preche .
His parischens . deuoutly wolde he teche .
Benygne he was . ⁊and wondyr diligent .
And in adủersite . full pacient .
And such he was preued . ofte sithes .
Full looth were hym . to curse for his tithes .
But rather . wolde he yeuen oute of doute .
Vn to his poor parisschens a boute .
Of his offryng . ⁊and of his substaūnce .
He couthe in litill þyng . haue suffisaūnce .
Wide was his parisch . ⁊and houses fer a sonder .
But he ne left / nought . for reyn ne thonder .
In sekenes . nor in myschef to vysite .
The ferthest in his parische . moche ⁊and lite .
Vp on his feet . ⁊and in his honde a staf
This noble ensample . vn to his scheep he yaf
That first he wrought . ⁊and afterwarde he taughte .
Oute of the gospell . he tho wordis kaughte .
And this figure he . addid therto .
That yf gold ruste . what schall yren do .
For yf a preest be foule . in whom we truste .
No wondyr is . a lewed man to ruste .
And schame it is . yf a preest take kepe .
A schitēm scheꝑperde . ⁊and a clene schepe .
Well ought a preest . ensample for to yeue
By his clennes . how his scheep schulde lyue .
He set nought . his bnfice to hire .
Ne lett his scheep . a combred in the myre .
And ren to londoıı̄un . vn to seynt powles .
To seken hym a chauntry . for sowles .
Or with a bretherhede . to ben with holde .
But dwellid at home . ⁊and kepte well his folde .
So that the wolf . ne made it not myscarie .
He was a schepperde . ⁊and not a mercernarie .
And though he holy were . ⁊and vertuous .
